problem: Existing object-navigation benchmarks cover few target categories and scene types (e.g., MP3D 21 objects, ProcTHOR 16 objects in 4 room types), so the open-vocabulary navigation ability of LVLMs/LLMs is unexplored and untrainable at scale.
motivation: Real-world navigation requires finding arbitrary objects in diverse scenes. The authors observe that cheap BFS shortest-path demonstrations, paired with templated CoT explanations, can teach an LVLM navigation without human demonstrations.
key_idea: Build a large, diverse AI2THOR scene dataset (DivScene) with Holodeck and GPT-4, sample BFS shortest-path episodes, and fine-tune Idefics 2 by imitation learning to output templated CoT explanations plus the next action (NatVLM).
insight: Removing the CoT explanation traces halves success (SR 54.94 -> 26.54 on test), and adding gold position labels without CoT does not help. So the explanation structure (position comparison, obstacle check, decision) is what teaches the rationale. Few-shot runs show 60% of the data already gives ~52 SR. The failure case shows limited exploration over long horizons because only recent history is available.
method: DivScene scene generation: 81 scene types (MIT Scenes plus additions), GPT-4 composes descriptions with 1-3 of 12 sampled attributes (ROUGE-L<0.8 filtering), and Holodeck builds 4,614 AI2THOR houses (4,506 train / 27 val / 81 test) using Objaverse assets (22,696 object types).

NavDiv episode sampling: discretize to a 0.25 m grid, randomly sample start and target (height 0.3-2.0 m, distinct types per house), find the shortest path with a rotation-penalized BFS, and derive MoveAhead/RotateLeft/RotateRight/Done actions; about 23K episodes with 5,707 target types.
Instruction compilation: prompt containing the task intro, target type and position, recommended grid position, agent pose, the last 8 steps of positions/actions, and the last 4 egocentric images.

CoT explanation response: manually written templates (compare position difference in the facing direction, check obstacles, then the decision) with coordinates filled in; three rotation scenarios and Done handled separately.
Data postprocessing: downsample MoveAhead to 25% and remove conflicting samples with identical inputs but different actions.
Imitation learning: behavior cloning (NLL) that fully fine-tunes Idefics 2 (8B), for 1 epoch, LR 2e-5, batch size 64, on 8 A100 GPUs.

setting.training_data: About 23K BFS shortest-path episodes (about 117K steps after postprocessing) from 4,506 synthetic DivScene houses, with templated CoT responses
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB (300x300, last 4 frames) plus agent position and rotation text, target position given
setting.action_space: Discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 90°, Done
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (Holodeck houses; zero-shot transfer to iTHOR, ProcTHOR, HM3D)
setting.privileged: Target object coordinates and the recommended nearest grid position are given in the prompt, along with agent GPS-like position and rotation; no map.

results: NatVLM reaches SR 57.41 (val) / 54.94 (test), about 20 points above GPT-4o (37.04 / 38.27), and doubles the same model fine-tuned without CoT (26.54 test). It transfers zero-shot to iTHOR (SR 72.79) and ProcTHOR (53.12) and gets SPL 34.1 on HM3D, above the listed baselines (VLFM 30.4).
limitations: Limited exploration and failures on long-horizon episodes because only recent history (8 steps/4 images) is used
Relies on given target coordinates and position information in the prompt, and templated CoT; evaluated in synthetic AI2THOR scenes only
HM3D comparison is not like-for-like with methods that use depth and other tools
